name: Shobab
overview: Shobab was a male member of the tribe of Judah and is uniquely identified in Scripture as one of the sons of King David. His mention is brief, with no additional notes or detailed narrative provided beyond his lineage. As a son of David, he is part of the royal family line significant in biblical history.
namesAndTitles: The name Shobab means "one who turns back, repents," reflecting a Hebrew proper name with a meaningful root. This meaning, while not explicitly tied to divine naming, may suggest a character trait or hoped-for quality. The name is recorded in 2 Samuel 5:14.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Shobab as a son of King David, confirming his royal lineage. He is also identified as a son of Bathsheba, David's wife, according to 1 Chronicles 3:5. Beyond these familial ties, no further relationships are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shobab's significance lies primarily in his place within the Davidic lineage, which is central to God's covenant promises and the messianic line culminating in Christ. Although the biblical record does not provide extensive details about his life or deeds, his inclusion among David's sons underscores the fulfillment of God's plan through David's family. This connection highlights the faithfulness of God in preserving the line from which Jesus, the Messiah, would ultimately come.
